title: LogEntry
description: One entry in the decision log's retrospective replay: real signals from about early 2026, a judgement attributed to the fictional Tracewell team, the real outcome by September 2026 with a dated source, and a qualitative calibration note. A composite: the entry as a whole is replay, and each part carries its own label. There is no verdict field (held / did not hold) and no field that could be tallied across entries; the calibration note is prose only. Shipped in data/log.js as an array.

originalSignals.description: The real signal or signals the past judgement was made on. Embedded rather than referenced to data/signals.js, because replay signals come from a different window and carry no relevance note.

calibrationNote.description: Qualitative prose such as 'threat reading held; timing was early'. Its label depends on who writes it (K-3, K-7).

role.description: R7, designed for and not built: the role of the team member the replayed judgement is attributed to. Absent in every fixture of this build.

pastJudgement.description: A judgement attributed to the fictional team as of asOfDate, but actually written on authoredOn, after the outcome was known. Both dates are carried so the after-the-fact authorship is visible in the data, not only in the replay statement (K-7). There is deliberately no intuition record: inventing one would be a fabrication.

asOfDate.description: The date whose knowledge the judgement represents. On or after the latest original signal, before the outcome (checked in the M8 unit test).

authoredOn.description: The date the judgement text was actually written.

source.description: Real, dated source. Its publishedOn must be later than every original signal's (checked in the M8 unit test). An invented outcome is a project-ending defect.
